limits: an OVER-refusal, not a hole: nothing gets through, a read-only line is turned away. `cp`, `robocopy`, `xcopy` and `tar` are not read-only to the kits' own classification -- rightly, they write their target -- so gate 1 collects EVERY word of such a stage, source and target alike. What it costs is a refused copy whose operand names a protected tree. The way round it is measured and cheap: spell the copy as a Python script under the round's scratch root (`C:/Offline Repos/v2-testbed/_round-scratch/<TSK-ID>/`), which CLAUDE.md prescribes anyway, or run it from a shell outside the session.
